react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a primary biological signal centred on methionine metabolism and its intersection with one-carbon unit cycling. In the RaMP multi-database ORA, Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) achieved the strongest FDR (3.75e-19) with 8 metabolites overlapping, followed by the Methionine de novo and salvage pathway (WP:WP3580, FDR = 1.16e-13) and KEGG Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270, FDR = 1.19e-13). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate / Methionine Metabolism, p = 3.36e-07) and hsa00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism, p = 0.0204). The m/z-direct Mummichog network method independently recovered methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism (MUMM, p = 0.0178) and glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (p = 0.0178) with 8 overlapping metabolites each, confirming the signal without relying on ID annotation. The three-way consensus establishes that the treatment perturbation dysregulates the methionine–homocysteine–SAM cycle, with S-adenosylmethionine (C00019), L-methionine (C00073) and homocysteine (C00155) as central driver metabolites. A secondary signal in arachidonic acid metabolism was detected by Mummichog (p = 0.0178), where 15-HETE (C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (C14823) point to active lipid peroxidation and eicosanoid biosynthesis, consistent with oxidative-stress-related treatment effects. Adenosine (C00212), choline (C00114) and L-glutamic acid (C00025) participate as cofactors linking the methionine cycle to folate metabolism and transsulfuration. This cross-paradigm concordance (ORA + m/z-direct + KEGG PSEA) strongly implicates methionine cycle dysregulation as the dominant pathway-level effect, with secondary arachidonic acid inflammatory signalling.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA identified Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the top pathway (FDR 3.75e-19, 8 of 57 metabolites hit from the input set) across Reactome, SMPDB, KEGG and WikiPathways namespaces. This result is independently confirmed by mummichog network-activity analysis, which returned Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) as its top hit (p = 0.0193, rank 0). The three-way consensus between RaMP ORA, mummichog network activity and Reactome Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (REACT:R-HSA-71291, FDR 7.96e-14) establishes glycine/serine/threonine/methionine metabolic perturbation as the dominant pathway-level effect. Driver metabolites verified from enrichment hit rosters include homocysteine, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-methionine, L-threonine, choline, L-glutamic acid, adenosine and lipoic acid as members of KEGG:map00260. Secondary convergence occurs at Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, rank 1, p = 0.0193) where 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742) appears as a member, and at Methionine and cysteine metabolism (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism, rank 2, p = 0.0193) where L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506) and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) are verified members.
